svg.text: Hiwonder Ackermann advanced kit · three identical plates, outline traced from Hiwonder's own CAD · 1.7 px/mm · front of vehicle to the LEFT · viewed from above, so the vehicle's own LEFT is at the BOTTOM of each plan
Deck gaps measured on the built kit 2026-09-20: lower 50 mm, upper 40 mm - two standoff lengths, not one. Fascia panels are 52 and 42 mm tall.
top face z 81.12 · STM32 carrier (boards A, B), 5 V split (board C) and the 5 V converter
top face z 29.12 · drive, battery, motor driver, WAGO 221-415 distribution and INA226 sensing
pattern 49.00 × 58.00 from NXP drill T11 - 0.06 mm out in x · dashed = its other 2 holes
fascia upper panel clamps here - 2 × M3×8 driven down from the top (MEC-07)
carrier 98 × 106: header row 1 at x 181.20 · 6 × M2.5 on 10 mm standoffs into existing holes (MEC-15)
battery leads and the 7.5 A main fuse route here
charge socket parks and ties in this channel
JGB37-520 ×2 from the CAD: ⌀37 gearbox outboard · ⌀33 can · encoder inboard
motors reach to 29.8 mm from the rear edge - switches stop ~8 mm short
the driver's rear 7 mm sits over the cans - clearance is vertical only, set by the spacer height
widest 120.4 mm at the front axle · 84.7 mm at the waist · 94.2 mm across the rear flat
fascia upper panel, 42 mm tall: USB-C · DE-9 · Mini-B
fascia lower panel, 52 mm tall: DRIVE / LOGIC switches
below plate 1: running gear, wheels, ground clearance - nothing mounted
WHAT IS FIXED, AND WHAT IS NOT
Measured on the built kit: 50 mm below, 40 mm above. The kit ships two standoff lengths; the
single-plate CAD only ever had the 50 and our 3-deck model repeated it for both gaps. The fascia
panels are therefore 52 and 42 mm tall and are no longer one blank (MEC-09).
Motors are mounted and the battery goes here: the heaviest mass low and central. Each motor reaches
from the centreline out past the plate edge to its wheel, 29.8–66.7 mm forward of the rear edge.
Deliberately blank. Compute boards, power stage and the Pi 5 all want deck space; nothing is committed
until the wiring and thermal picture settle.
The fascia already constrains all three
Purple rings are the fascia clamp holes (y 124.54, x −41.34 / +46.30) and yellow are the four standoffs.
Every other hole and slot is drawn from the CAD - 96 of them per plate - so a board can be placed on
real fixings. Plate 2's single M3×12 clamps both panels at once (MEC-07).
Keep clear of the rear on plate 1
Switch bodies protrude ~25 mm into the lower gap and the motors start 29.8 mm in, leaving about 8 mm
between them - confirm with the switches in hand before printing (MEC-07).
The servo box is traced from the CAD. The pack is 63 × 77 × 20 mm (2026-09-20) - 20 mm tall clears any
plausible lower gap with room for the strap and the leads.
Size or fixing NOT resolved - do not commit this position yet
M2.5 screw into an existing chassis hole - washer spans the 0.34 mm slop (MEC-10)
M3 screw into a 3.18 mm chassis hole - close fit, ease the part not the plate
Fascia clamp hole, M3, present on every deck (MEC-07)
M3 through a 4.29 mm chassis slot - free to slide along it, washer under the head
Cable tie through the part's own hole into the slot or cutout under it - no chassis hole exists there
20 mm hook-and-loop strap - up through one chassis slot, over the pack, down the other, closed underneath
